messages:
nisha: Heads-up — compliance pinged asking if we can guarantee immediate and verifiable erasure of KV prefix caches when a tenant requests data deletion. They mentioned Hosted, Dedicated, and Private scenarios for contracts.
ben: Short rundown: Hosted = we control the nodes so we can scrub quickly. Dedicated = we still manage infra but there are reserved pools and longer retention windows; Private = customer-managed so we can't unilaterally wipe things on their hardware.
olga: We should define "erase" precisely. Is it zeroing memory, truncating mmapped files, deleting on-disk segments, expiring backups/snapshots, or removing telemetry traces? Compliance expects an auditable proof-of-deletion.
sam: Also think about in-flight requests: if we tombstone prefixes, we must ensure no outstanding request will read a stale KV after the erase. Race between erase and ongoing generation could leak context.
compliance-bot: Reminder: SOC/CCPA/DSAR workflows require response windows and audit trails. For some regs, a best-effort scrub is insufficient — they want evidence and timelines.
ben: Proposed model with tradeoffs:
- Mode A (Immediate, strong): Synchronous RPC to all active serving nodes + block new reads for prefix until scrub acked. Truncates/madvise-wipe on-disk shards, zeroes mmapped memory, deletes backups. High latency and throughput impact.
- Mode B (Fast, probabilistic): Mark prefix as erased in metadata (generation++) and reject new reads; background workers scrub replicas and disk lazily. Lower 99p impact, but not instant. Provide audit events with expected completion window.
- Mode C (Hosted-only crypto shortcut): If cache on disk is encrypted with per-tenant DEK, rotate/retire the tenant key (crypto-shred) — instant logical erase for on-disk content but still need to scrub memory and backups separately.
olga: Crypto-shred is attractive for disk-backed caches. If we ensure every cache file is encrypted with a tenant-specific key that we control, rotating/forgetting the key gives strong guarantees without immediate IO. But tradeoffs:
- Need to ensure keys are actually per-tenant (storage overhead, KMS/API complexity).
- For Dedicated we manage keys so this works; for Private we can't hold customer keys in most cases.
- Memory contents still need wiping.
sam: For correctness around in-flight requests: add a prefix generation/version vector attached to every request. Serving nodes check request.generation == prefix.generation. On erase we increment generation and cause mismatch — in-flight requests with older generation either fail and retry or continue but without access to evicted data. That avoids returning old KVs after erase.
ben: Example erase API sketch (internal):
``` 
POST /internal/cache/erase
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "prefix": "conv-987",
  "mode": "immediate", // immediate | best_effort | crypto-shred
  "request_id": "uuid-..."
}
```
Response would include list of nodes contacted and scrub status.
compliance-bot: Audit requirements: store an immutable deletion record with request_id, mode, timestamp, impacted nodes, and scrub checksums. We may need a signed attestation for enterprise contracts.
nisha: Operational concerns:
- Immediate mode = spike in RPC fanout and disk IO. Need throttling and operator guardrails.
- Background scrub needs a GC queue with backoff and visibility in Console (progress bars, expected completion time).
- Need a way to escalate: customer can request emergency wipe (legal/sales flow) that runs immediate mode with on-call approval.
olga: Implementation plan proposals:
1) Short-term (2w): metadata-only API. Implement generation bump + reject-path; background cleaner marks and scrubs asynchronously. Expose audit event and Console UI showing status. This covers many DSAR timelines.
2) Mid-term (6-8w): add per-tenant DEK support for disk caches in Hosted/Dedicated and integrate with KMS key lifecycle to allow crypto-shred. Add immediate-mode orchestration with throttles.
3) Long-term (Q3+): offline verification tool to scan backups/snapshots, plus a signed attestation feature for enterprise customers.
ben: Edge cases:
- Multi-tenant shared cache shards: when a shard contains entries for many tenants, we must avoid full-shard wipe. Prefer per-prefix encrypted blobs or store tenant-id->file mapping.
- Snapshots & S3 backups: need lifetime/retention policy and a background job to delete objects; but object deletion in S3 is eventual and may be cached by CDN.
- Private deployments: we provide the API and a reference scrub script, but customer must run it or grant Redwood remote scrub permissions in contract.
sam: Testing plan:
- Unit: generation bump + request mismatch path.
- Integration: simulate large fanout erase across 200 nodes, measure 99p latency impact.
- Chaos: kill nodes mid-scrub and ensure metadata still reflects pending work and retries.
nisha: Decisions from this thread (draft):
- Implement metadata-only generation-based erase immediately (short-term).
- Add internal /internal/cache/erase endpoint and Console visibility.
- Scope per-tenant DEK for Hosted/Dedicated as a follow-up (mid-term).
- For Private, require customer opt-in for remote scrubs; provide docs and reference tools.
Action items:
- nisha: write short RFC for API + Console flows (due EOD Fri).
- ben: prototype crypto-shred on local dev cluster and measure disk overhead (start Mon).
- olga: draft audit schema and attestation requirements with compliance (sync Tue).
- sam: add generation checks to serving path and add unit tests (PR next week).
compliance-bot: Logged request: DSAR-2026-09-T1. Please attach RFC link when ready.
ben: One more note — we should expose an "erase_state" metric per-tenant so SRE can alert on stuck scrubs.
nisha: Thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link in this thread once it's up. :thumbsup:
